To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
EBV DNA was found in all 23 African Burkitt's tumors, 18 out 23 African NPC's, and 8 of 24 other tumors.
EBV DNA was detected by DNA-DNA re-association kinetics in 23 out of 24 Burkitt's lymphomas from Africa, 18 out 23 African NPC, and 8 out 24 other African cancers.
23 of 24 African tumors, including 23 of 23 NPC, contained EBV genomes and that EBV genomes were present in 8 of 24 other tumors from African patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the presence of EBV DNA in tumors.
the detection of EBV DNA in biopsied human tumors by DNA-DNA reannealing kinetics and cRNA hybridization methods.
the detection of EBV DNA in human tumor biopsies and with the relationship between EBV DNA and the development of tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EBV is present in the majority of African Burkitt's tumors and NPC but not in American Burkitt's tumors.
EBV DNA is present in 100% of African Burkitt's tumors and NPC, 50% of other African tumors, 0% of American Burkitt tumors, and 12% of other American tumors.
EBV is not found in the great majority of American tumors, but is found in 100% of African Burkitt's tumors, and 75% of African NPC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EBV DNA is present in 50% of African Burkitt's and NPC tumors, and 3% of other African tumors.

1) African Burkitt's tumor and African NPC contain 1 to 10 EBV genomes per cell, 2) American Burkitt's tumors contain less than 1 EBV DNA genome per cell, 3) other African tumors and American tumors contain 1 to less than 10 EBV DNA genomes per cell, and 4) the EBV DNA genome is present in all of the tumors tested in a latent state.
EBV is present in 50% to 60% of all African tumors tested, but is present in less than 5% of tumors in other areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EBV is a common human pathogen and is present in human tumors.
EBV is present in many human cancers, and the presence of the virus may have some role in the etiology of these tumors.
the EBV genome is present in the majority of African NPC biopsies and a substantial proportion of other African tumors, but not in most American NPC biopsies or American tumors.
